title: Project Instruction File Triage
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Evaluation activity in which learners judge each of eleven lines of an illustrative draft project instruction file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) for a SAR ADC project as a Goal, a Convention, a Constraint, or Does not belong. Each line has one attempt in a fixed order, with feedback that states the correct label and a one-sentence reason. The run ends with a score out of 11, a mastery statement at 9 of 11, and where the content of each line that does not belong should live instead.

educational.topic: Writing project instruction files for coding agents
learningObjectives: Judge each of eleven lines of a draft instruction file as a goal, a convention, a constraint, or not belonging in the file, with at least 9 of 11 judged correctly
prerequisites: Project instruction file, project goals, project conventions, and project constraints, as defined in the section Project Instruction Files of Chapter 5

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key, and the label buttons report their selected state with aria-pressed; correct and incorrect judgments are marked with a check mark or an X and stated in words as well as in blue and orange; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Goal / Convention / Constraint / Does not belong
controls.purpose: Selects a label for the highlighted line. The selection can be changed until Submit is pressed.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Enabled once a label is selected. Commits the single attempt for the highlighted line, shows the feedback, and highlights the next line.

controls.label: See Score
controls.purpose: Shown after line 11 is judged. Shows the final score, the mastery result, and where each line that does not belong should live instead.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Line-by-line four-way judgment against explicit criteria (durable, checkable, safe) with immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Is this line a goal, a convention, a constraint, or not worth putting in the file?
Will this line still be true next week?
Would this line be safe in a committed file?
commonMisconceptions: Anything useful to say to an agent belongs in the instruction file
A vague exhortation such as be careful is a constraint
A credential in a private repository is safe to include
assessmentOpportunities: At least 9 of 11 lines judged correctly on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
The learner can name where each removed line belongs instead: a log, nowhere, or a secrets store
Reading the draft file as a whole is exploration, not evidence
